title: Form 40: Deferring Tax on Overseas Retirement Savings for Returning NRIs
description: Indian tax residents who previously lived abroad can use Form 40 to defer tax on their foreign retirement accounts. This form allows tax to be paid only when .

faq.a: Form 40 is a declaration form filed with the Indian Income Tax Department by returning NRIs to defer tax on income accruing in specified foreign retirement funds until withdrawal.

faq.q: Which countries' retirement funds are covered by Form 40?
faq.a: Form 40 primarily covers retirement funds in countries like the US (e.g., 401k, IRA), UK (e.g., SIPP), Canada (e.g., RRSP), and Australia (e.g., Superannuation), subject to DTAA provisions.

faq.q: Does Form 40 exempt me from paying tax on my foreign retirement savings?
faq.a: No, Form 40 does not provide an exemption. It only defers the tax liability, meaning you pay tax on the withdrawals when you receive them, rather than on the annual accruals.

faq.q: When do I need to file Form 40?
faq.a: You generally need to file Form 40 by the due date for filing your Income Tax Return for the financial year in which you become a tax resident in India.

faq.q: What happens if I don't file Form 40?
faq.a: If you don't file Form 40 and are a tax resident, the annual accruals in your foreign retirement fund could potentially be taxed in India, leading to a higher tax burden.

faq.q: Can I file Form 40 for any foreign investment account?
faq.a: No, Form 40 is specifically for certain *retirement funds* that meet the criteria laid out in CBDT notifications and relevant DTAAs, not for general investment accounts.
